title: New Research Calls for Changes to Breast Cancer Screening for Young Women
subtitle: Current guidelines in England may miss 95% of young women who will develop the disease, according to a new study.

summary.en: Recent research suggests that current medical guidelines for breast cancer screening in England are not effective for women under 50. The study shows that the existing system misses nearly all young women who will later develop the disease. Experts argue that the current focus on family history is too narrow. Researchers suggest that new, more detailed assessment tools could help find high-risk patients earlier. However, officials warn that implementing these changes will require balancing costs and medical resources.
summary.zh: 近期研究指出，英國目前的乳癌篩檢醫療指導方針對五十歲以下女性並不有效。研究顯示，現行系統幾乎漏掉了所有未來會罹患此病的年輕女性。專家認為，目前過度聚焦於家族病史的作法過於狹隘。研究人員建議，採用更新且更詳盡的評估工具，有助於更早發現高風險病患。然而，官員警告，落實這些變革將需要權衡成本與醫療資源。

paragraphs.en: New research has highlighted a significant gap in how breast cancer risk is identified in young women. According to The Guardian Health, the current guidelines used by family doctors in England fail to spot 95% of women under 50 who will go on to develop the disease within a decade. This finding has led to urgent calls for a review of how medical professionals assess risk and decide who needs further testing or specialist care.
paragraphs.zh: 一項新研究凸顯出在辨識年輕女性罹患乳癌風險方面存在顯著落差。根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）報導，英國家庭醫師目前所採用的指導方針，無法篩檢出百分之九十五在十年內會罹患此病的五十歲以下女性。這項發現引發了緊急呼籲，要求重新檢視醫療專業人員評估風險的方式，以及判定哪些人需要進一步檢查或專科照護的標準。

paragraphs.en: Breast cancer is the most common form of cancer globally and remains a leading cause of death for women under 50. Currently, doctors in England follow criteria set by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) to decide which patients should receive extra screening. These guidelines rely heavily on a person’s family history of the disease. However, the study from the University of Cambridge and the Institute of Cancer Research (ICR) suggests that this approach is no longer enough to protect younger patients.
paragraphs.zh: 乳癌是全球最常見的癌症類型，也是五十歲以下女性的主要死因之一。目前，英國醫師遵循「國家健康與照護卓越研究院」（Nice）所制定的標準，來決定哪些病患應接受額外篩檢。這些指導方針過度依賴個人的家族病史。然而，來自劍橋大學（University of Cambridge）與癌症研究所（ICR）的研究指出，這種方式已不足以保護年輕病患。

paragraphs.en: The research, published in the British Journal of Cancer, found that 73% of women under 50 who develop breast cancer have no family history of the disease at all. Because the current system focuses so much on family history, it ignores the majority of young women who are at risk. Dr. Juliet Usher-Smith from the University of Cambridge explained that the medical community needs to improve how it identifies these women. By finding those at high risk earlier, doctors have more options to treat the disease or even prevent it from starting.
paragraphs.zh: 這項發表於《英國癌症期刊》（British Journal of Cancer）的研究發現，百分之七十三罹患乳癌的五十歲以下女性，完全沒有家族病史。由於現行系統過於側重家族病史，導致大多數處於風險中的年輕女性被忽略。劍橋大學的厄舍-史密斯醫師（Dr. Juliet Usher-Smith）解釋，醫療界必須改善辨識這些女性的方式。透過更早找出高風險族群，醫師將有更多選擇來治療疾病，甚至預防疾病發生。

paragraphs.en: To address this, researchers compared the current Nice guidelines with a new risk assessment system called Boadicea. This system, funded by Cancer Research UK, looks at a wider range of factors, including a woman’s lifestyle, reproductive history, and genetics. When using this new method, experts were able to identify eight times as many women in the younger age group who were likely to develop breast cancer. This suggests that a more detailed approach could significantly improve early detection rates.
paragraphs.zh: 為了改善此問題，研究人員將現行的 Nice 指導方針與一套名為 Boadicea 的新型風險評估系統進行比較。這套由「英國癌症研究協會」（Cancer Research UK）資助的系統，考量了更廣泛的因素，包括女性的生活型態、生育史及遺傳基因。使用這種新方法時，專家能辨識出的高風險年輕女性人數是過去的八倍。這顯示更詳盡的評估方式能顯著提升早期發現率。

paragraphs.en: Despite these promising results, experts acknowledge that changing the system is not simple. Prof. Montserrat García-Closas of the ICR noted that there is a difficult balance to strike. While the current Nice criteria are easy for doctors to use in a busy office, they miss many women who are at an elevated risk—meaning a higher chance of developing the disease. On the other hand, using a full risk assessment that includes genetic testing would place a heavy burden on the healthcare system’s limited resources.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管研究結果令人振奮，專家也承認改變系統並非易事。癌症研究所的賈西亞-克洛薩斯教授（Prof. Montserrat García-Closas）指出，這其中存在難以拿捏的平衡。雖然現行的 Nice 標準讓醫師在繁忙的門診中容易操作，但卻漏掉了許多風險較高（意即罹病機率較大）的女性。另一方面，若採用包含基因檢測在內的全面風險評估，將會對醫療體系有限的資源造成沉重負擔。

paragraphs.en: Ultimately, the decision to update these guidelines will involve a trade-off. Health officials must weigh the practical costs of collecting more data against the potential benefits of catching cancer earlier. Dr. Simon Vincent, chief scientific officer at Breast Cancer Now, stated that finding new ways to identify women at increased risk is vital. He believes that better detection could lead to more successful treatments and save lives.
paragraphs.zh: 歸根究柢，更新這些指導方針的決定將涉及取捨。衛生官員必須權衡收集更多數據的實際成本，與更早發現癌症的潛在效益。乳癌防治組織「Breast Cancer Now」的科學長文森特博士（Dr. Simon Vincent）表示，尋找辨識高風險女性的新方法至關重要。他相信更完善的檢測能帶來更成功的治療，並挽救生命。

paragraphs.en: This study follows recent reports about a rise in cancer cases among younger people. As previously covered, researchers at the Washington University School of Medicine have been studying why cancer is becoming more common in those under 50. Their work suggests that younger generations may be experiencing faster biological aging, which could be a factor in the rise of these diseases. Together, these findings point to a growing need for medical guidelines that better reflect the realities of health for younger adults.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究延續了近期關於年輕族群癌症病例增加的報導。如先前所述，華盛頓大學醫學院（Washington University School of Medicine）的研究人員一直在探討為何癌症在五十歲以下族群中變得更為普遍。他們的研究顯示，年輕世代可能經歷了較快的生物性老化，這可能是導致疾病增加的因素之一。綜合這些發現，醫療界愈發需要能更真實反映年輕成人健康狀況的指導方針。

paragraphs.en: As the debate continues, the focus remains on how to provide the best care without overwhelming the medical system. For now, the call for a review of the Nice criteria remains a top priority for researchers who hope to turn these findings into better patient outcomes. The goal is to ensure that young women are not left behind by outdated screening methods, giving them the best possible chance to fight the disease before it becomes a serious threat.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著辯論持續進行，焦點仍是如何在不拖垮醫療體系的前提下提供最佳照護。目前，要求重新檢視 Nice 標準的呼聲，仍是研究人員的首要任務，他們希望能將這些發現轉化為更好的病患預後。目標是確保年輕女性不會因過時的篩檢方法而被遺漏，讓她們在疾病演變成嚴重威脅前，擁有對抗疾病的最佳機會。

Understanding these biological changes could be key to addressing this growing health concern.

quiz.question: According to the research findings, what percentage of women under 50 who develop breast cancer lack a family history of the disease?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，研究發現 73% 的 50 歲以下乳癌患者並沒有家族病史。選項 A 是錯誤的數據；選項 C 的 95% 是指現行篩檢指南漏掉的風險比例，而非無家族病史的比例；選項 D 為文中提到的年齡分界，與題目要求的數據無關。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why might the healthcare system be hesitant to immediately adopt the Boadicea assessment system?

options.A: It has been proven less accurate than the current Nice guidelines.
options.B: It focuses exclusively on genetic testing, which is not yet available.
options.C: It requires more comprehensive data collection, which could strain limited medical resources.
options.D: It is designed only for older women, making it unsuitable for the target demographic.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第五段，專家指出雖然 Boadicea 能更精準評估風險，但若要進行包含基因檢測的完整評估，會對醫療系統有限的資源造成沉重負擔。選項 A 與文意相反，Boadicea 其實更精準；選項 B 錯誤，因為該系統包含生活方式等多種因素；選項 D 與文章強調的「年輕族群」目標不符。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the phrase 'difficult balance to strike' mean in the context of updating medical guidelines?

options.A: A challenging trade-off between competing priorities.
options.B: A physical struggle to move medical equipment.
options.C: An argument between two groups of researchers.
options.D: A process of choosing the cheapest option regardless of quality.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，strike a balance 指的是在兩種衝突的需求（如：篩檢的精準度 vs. 醫療系統的成本與執行難度）之間找到平衡點。選項 B 將詞組誤解為物理動作；選項 C 雖然提到專家意見，但並非該詞組的定義；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章強調的是效益與成本的權衡，而非單純追求便宜。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding breast cancer screening for young women?

options.A: Family history is the only reliable indicator for breast cancer risk in young women.
options.B: The rise in cancer cases among the young is solely due to faster biological aging.
options.C: Current screening methods are highly effective and require no further changes.
options.D: Existing guidelines are outdated and need to incorporate broader risk factors to better protect younger women.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。文章主旨旨在呼籲更新現行篩檢標準，因為現行過度依賴家族病史的系統已無法有效保護年輕女性，應納入如生活方式與基因等更多元指標。選項 A 與文意完全相反；選項 B 僅是文中提到的其中一個因素，非主旨；選項 C 與文章開頭提到的「95% 漏診率」衝突，顯然是不正確的。
